item.title: GB win doubles decider to reach Davis Cup semi-finals for first time since 2019
item.description: Great Britain advance to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski win a decisive doubles tie against Germany in Bologna.

item.title: Knee surgery rules Sinner out of Australian Open
item.description: Jannik Sinner is ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee.

item.title: 'It was ruthless'- GB's Patten on ending top-ranked partnership with Heliovaara
item.description: Britain's Henry Patten agrees he was "ruthless" in splitting with doubles partner and close friend Harri Heliovaara, just days after they received the year-end world number one trophy.

item.title: Rinderknech denies refusing doping test
item.description: French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test.

item.title: 'I miss being on court' - Sinner has 'minor surgery' on knee
item.description: World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins.

item.title: 84 days, four titles, one historic feat - Alcaraz's remarkable return
item.description: Over the past 84 days, Carlos Alcaraz has won four titles, and he beat world number one Alexander Zverev to make history at the ATP Finals on Sunday.

item.title: Alcaraz outplays Zverev for first ATP Finals triumph
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz ends his wait for a first ATP Finals title as he outplays world number one Alexander Zverev in Turin.

item.title: 'Right time' for Smith exit - but Murray not ready for role
item.description: Leon Smith steps down as Britain's Davis Cup captain after almost 17 years, but "standout candidate" Andy Murray is unlikely to replace him.

item.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev in ATP Finals title decider
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz will face world number one Alexander Zverev for the ATP Finals title after completing a superb comeback victory against Ben Shelton.

item.title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m & delays doubles cuts decision
item.description: The men's ATP Tour promises players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but delays a decision on hotly-disputed changes to doubles until next month.

item.title: Alcaraz puts aside injury concerns to take apart Cobolli
item.description: A ruthless Carlos Alcaraz puts aside his injury concerns to dismantle Flavio Cobolli and ensure a perfect record in the ATP Finals group stages.

item.title: Tennis the saviour for player who tried to take own life before Wimbledon
item.description: Swiss player Leandro Riedi tried to take his own life days before playing at Wimbledon in 2024. Now he wants to tell his story.

item.title: Unbeaten Zverev hopes to be 'pain-free' after overcoming Fils at ATP Finals
item.description: World number one Alexander Zverev says he will do "everything I can to be pain-free" after hurting his ankle during his ATP Finals victory over Arthur Fils.

item.title: Zverev to defend himself against fresh lawsuit
item.description: Lawyers for world number one Alexander Zverev say he will defend himself against a lawsuit which alleges he misrepresented the outcome of a domestic abuse trial.

item.title: Australia's Barty elected into Tennis Hall of Fame
item.description: Three-time Grand Slam winner Ash Barty will be elected into the International Tennis Hall of Fame at a ceremony in August next year.

item.title: Alcaraz continues winning run despite injury concern
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz continues his sensational late-season form as he outclasses world number five Daniil Medvedev to confirm his progress at the ATP Finals.

item.title: Ruthless Zverev through to ATP Finals knockout stage
item.description: World number one Alexander Zverev produces a serving masterclass to defeat Ben Shelton and qualify for the ATP Finals knockout stage with a match to spare.

item.title: Skupski and Patten win to send GB into Davis Cup semi-finals
item.description: Great Britain's Neal Skupski and Henry Patten produce a stunning victory against Germany's Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz to win the decisive doubles match and secure Great Britain's place in the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019.

item.title: Zverev too good for Fery in Davis Cup quarter-final
item.description: World number one Alexander Zverev shows his class as he comfortably beats Great Britain's Arthur Fery in straight sets to draw Germany level at 1-1 in their Davis Cup quarter final tie.

item.title: Norrie holds nerve to beat Struff in Davis Cup quarter-final
item.description: British number two Cameron Norrie gives Great Britain the perfect start to their Davis Cup quarter-final against Germany, as he beats Jan-Lennard Struff in three sets in the opening match of their tie in Bolgona.

item.title: Teenage sensation Andreeva wins WTA Finals
item.description: Nineteen-year-old Miira Andreeva beat Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 to win the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, capping an outstanding week with a straight-set victory.

item.title: Andreeva beats world number two Sabalenka to reach WTA semis
item.description: Russia's Mirra Andreeva beats world number two and second seed Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals.

item.title: GB's Patten criticises ATP chairman and CEO for absence
item.description: Britain's top-ranked doubles player Henry Patten criticises the ATP's chairman and CEO for missing the year-end world number one trophy presentation.

item.title: Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title
item.description: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva caps her stellar season with a hard-fought victory over Elina Svitolina to win the WTA Finals.

item.title: 'Best I've felt' - Alcaraz makes statement start at ATP Finals
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz warns his rivals he has never felt better at this stage of a season after beginning his ATP Finals bid with a statement win over Frances Tiafoe.

item.title: Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina'
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka apologises and denies claims she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing in Russian during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian.

item.title: Svitolina races into WTA Finals showpiece against Andreeva
item.description: Elina Svitolina drops just three games as she thrashes Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva.

item.title: Sabalenka's season ended by Svitolina at WTA Finals
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka's season ends in disappointment as Elina Svitolina beats the former world number one to claim her place in the knockout stage at the WTA Finals.

item.title: Alcaraz beats Shelton to win first Paris Masters
item.description: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz wins his first Paris Masters defeating world number four Ben Shelton 7-6 (7-5) 7-5 at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre.

item.title: Dart reacts to her first WTA title after 'incredible week'
item.description: Speaking to BBC Sport, Harriet Dart says it's been an "incredible week" after coming through qualifying to win the Guangzhou Open, the first WTA Tour singles title of her career.

item.title: Wawrinka retires in front of home crowd after defeat to Lehecka
item.description: Three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka retires in front of his home crowd after losing in straight sets to Jiri Lehecka in the opening round of the Swiss Indoors in Basel.

item.title: Kartal misses out on Wuhan Open title against Chwalinska
item.description: Britain's Sonay Kartal misses out on the Wuhan Open title after a 2-6 6-4 6-2 defeat by French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska. The final caps a remarkable run for Kartal in only her third event since returning from a six-month lay-off with a back injury.

item.title: Kartal reflects on becoming British number one
item.description: Sonay Kartal reflects on becoming British number one after reaching the final of the Wuhan Open.

item.title: History made as Zheng becomes first Chinese woman to win China Open
item.description: Zheng Qinwen makes history in Beijing as she beats Mirra Andreeva in straight sets to win the China Open, becoming the first Chinese woman to win the tournament.

item.title: Djokovic ends trophy drought with victory in China
item.description: Novak Djokovic wins the China Open for a seventh time after Alex de Minaur retires in the final in Beijing, as the Serb wins the 102nd title of his career.

item.title: Sabalenka crashes out of China Open after defeat by Bartunkova
item.description: World number two Aryna Sabalenka crashes out of the China Open after a surprise straight-set defeat by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova.

item.title: Bouzkova beats Kartal as Czech Republic take BJK Cup lead over GB
item.description: Sonay Kartal is narrowly beaten by Marie Bouzkova in the first singles match as Czech Republic take a 1-0 lead over Great Britain in the Billie Jean King Cup.

item.title: GB qualify for Davis Cup Finals after doubles win
item.description: Great Britain qualify for the Davis Cup Finals after taking an unassailable 3-0 lead over Ecuador as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski beat Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo 6-3 6-4.

item.title: 'That is a stunner' - the best shots from GB v Ecuador in Fery's Davis Cup win
item.description: Watch the best shots from Arthur Fery's victory over Alvaro Guillen Meza as he helps Great Britain take a 2-0 lead over Ecuador in their Davis Cup qualifying match.

item.title: Zverev wins US Open to earn second Grand Slam victory
item.description: Alexander Zverev wins the second Grand Slam of his career by beating Ben Shelton 6-3, 6-6 (7-6), 5-7, 6-2 in the final of the US Open.

item.title: 'I don't fear for my safety from online abuse - because we're so used to it'
item.description: Britain's Jodie Burrage speaks to BBC Sport about the online abuse she received after her recent defeat - and why it no longer comes as a surprise.

item.title: Zverev becomes deserved world number one - but sense of discomfort remains
item.description: Alexander Zverev has been the best player in the world in men's tennis this year - but a sense of discomfort remains.

item.title: How Dart revived career with help of Wimbledon champion
item.description: Britain's Harriet Dart knows people doubted whether she would ever win a WTA title, but says the belief of her coach Marion Bartoli helped achieve the best week of her career.

item.title: The rising French star whose dad won Rugby World Cup with England
item.description: Felix Balshaw is the son of an English Rugby World Cup winner - but is representing France as he climbs the world tennis rankings.

item.title: Inside British number one Kartal's remarkable comeback
item.description: Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not brush her teeth without "being in agony" - now she's the British number one after three events back from a long-term back injury.

item.title: From struggling to walk to lifting trophy - how Rybakina triumphed
item.description: Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.

item.title: No Brits left in US Open singles - but are there reasons to be positive?
item.description: There will be no British interest in the second week of another Grand Slam at the US Open - but is it all doom and gloom?

item.title: What are the heat rules at Wimbledon?
item.description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains the heat rules at Wimbledon and when it is and is not safe to play in the heat

item.title: Who are the Wimbledon record-holders?
item.description: Our Ask Me Anything team looks at who has won the most Wimbledon singles and doubles titles.

item.title: What do hand signals mean in Wimbledon doubles?
item.description: Our Ask Me Anything team explains what the player hand signals mean in doubles matches.

item.title: What is Wimbledon's Last 8 Club?
item.description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team looks at what Wimbledon's Last 8 Club is and how players qualify for it.

item.title: How is the Wimbledon schedule decided? Your questions answered
item.description: Our Ask Me Anything team answer your questions about the Wimbledon schedule.
